public_rationale: The January 2021 MMLU paper reports 32.4% accuracy for fine-tuned GPT-2 and 43.9% for GPT-3 X-Large, a gain of 11.5 percentage points [e1]. OpenAI's March 2023 report gives GPT-4 a score of 86.4%, a further gain of 42.5 points [e1, e2]. OpenAI's April 11, 2024 evaluation record reports 86.5–86.7% for the April 9 Turbo snapshot, only 0.1–0.3 points above the original GPT-4 result [e2, e3]. These reported gains support the historical pattern of a substantially smaller final increase, but differing evaluation methods limit its value as evidence of diminishing returns [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The records do not compare all four models under one protocol: GPT-2 was fine-tuned, GPT-3 used few-shot prompting, GPT-4 used five-shot prompting, and Turbo used zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting [e1, e2, e3].
These MMLU results alone do not establish diminishing returns to training resources, a general slowdown across capabilities, or limits on future improvement [e1, e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: MMLU gains from GPT-4 to GPT-4 Turbo are small compared with earlier generational jumps, tentatively evidencing diminishing returns.

statement.excerpt: Huge jump from GPT-2 to GPT-3. Huge jump from GPT-3 to GPT-4 … and not so much for GPT-4 (13 months ago) to GPT-4 Turbo (just released). It’s hard not to see this plot as tentative evidence for the hypothesis of diminishing returns.
statement.document_title: Evidence that LLMs are reaching a point of diminishing returns - and what that might mean

our_interpretation: Compare absolute percentage-point gains on MMLU across the named models, using the largest GPT-3 model and the April 2024 GPT-4 Turbo snapshot.
The ordinary reading is that the last reported gain is substantially smaller than both earlier gains. No precise threshold for 'huge' or 'not so much' is supplied.

Assess the historical score pattern and its tentative evidential value. This is not a prediction that future models will stop improving or a demonstrated relationship between training expenditure and capability.
The target covers the named historical generations through the post date. Its start is unspecified because the passage gives no starting calendar date.
Evaluation methods must be examined. Differences limit the strength of the inference even when the reported percentage-accuracy pattern is clear.
criteria.support_condition: Published MMLU results show a substantially smaller GPT-4-to-April-2024-Turbo accuracy gain than both earlier generational gains, with methodological qualifications consistent with describing the pattern as tentative evidence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable published results show that the GPT-4-to-April-2024-Turbo gain is similar to or larger than either earlier generational gain, undermining the stated historical pattern.

evidence.explanation: Table 2 reports GPT-4 MMLU accuracy of 86.4% with five-shot evaluation. Compared with the GPT-3 result in e1, the published increase is 42.5 percentage points.

The initial release reports April Turbo MMLU scores of 86.5% with the chatgpt prompt and 86.7% with the assistant prompt, only 0.1–0.3 points above e2. It describes zero-shot chain-of-thought evaluation and warns about prompting sensitivity, limiting comparison with GPT-4's five-shot result.
